get.description: Returns change history for a specific entity

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the company.

parameters.name: entity_type
parameters.description: The type of entity to retrieve change history for

parameters.name: entity_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the entity to retrieve change history for

parameters.name: filters[change_type]
parameters.description: Filter by change type (e.g., asset_updated_asset_name)

parameters.name: filters[changed_by]
parameters.description: Filter by user who made the change

parameters.name: filters[changed_at]
parameters.description: Changed at filter (date range format: YYYY-MM-DD...YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ...YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ)

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sorting criteria in minus-based order format. Default sort order is ascending. Prefix with minus (-) for descending order. Default sort is by changed_at in descending order. Supports both snake_case and camelCase. Valid field: changed_at (or changedAt).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Zero-based page index (0..N)

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of items per page to be returned

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Locale for localized response messages (for example: en, fr-FR, pseudo)

200.description: Change history records retrieved successfully. Response varies based on entity_type.

Link.description: Links to related pages (first, prev, next, last)

oneOf.description: Response for entity_type=asset - returns asset change history records

data.description: Array of asset change history records

id.description: Unique identifier for the change history record

event_id.description: Unique identifier for the change event (groups related changes)

entity_id.description: The ID of the entity (asset) that was changed

operation.description: The type of operation performed: c (create), u (update), d (delete)

change_type.description: Specific type of change that occurred (e.g., asset_updated_asset_name, asset_created, asset_deleted)

additionalProperties.description: The state of the changed field(s) before the modification. Null for create operations.

before.description: The state of the changed field(s) before the modification. Null for create operations.

additionalProperties.description: The state of the changed field(s) after the modification. Null for delete operations.

after.description: The state of the changed field(s) after the modification. Null for delete operations.

company_id.description: The company ID the entity belongs to

project_id.description: The project ID the entity belongs to (null for company-level entities)

oneOf.title: asset

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("localhost:8080")

headers = {
    'Procore-Company-Id': "SOME_INTEGER_VALUE",
    'Accept-Language': "SOME_STRING_VALUE"
    }

conn.request("GET", "/rest/v2.0/companies/1234/assets/%7Bentity_type%7D/%7Bentity_id%7D/history?filters%5Bchange_type%5D=SOME_STRING_VALUE&filters%5Bchanged_by%5D=SOME_STRING_VALUE&filters%5Bchanged_at%5D=SOME_STRING_VALUE&sort=SOME_STRING_VALUE&page=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE&per_page=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE", headers=headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))
